sources: Reuters wire; Serhiy Beskrestnov (adviser to Zelensky, on Telegram); Ukrainian Defence Ministry source + two officials (via Reuters); Donald Trump (Friday remarks); Downing Street readout (PM Andy Burnham - Trump call)
fault_line: Did Trump/Musk hand Russia an advantage by capping Ukraine's drone-defence network (betrayal) -- or is this just a private company's commercial throttle (fair business)?

sections.what_happened: Reuters: five Ukrainian officials familiar with the matter say speed restrictions on Starlink that disrupt drone connections (drones faster than 160 km/h) persist, contradicting Trump's Thursday claim of full restoration. Beskrestnov (Telegram): 'We are currently not observing any lifting of speed limits on Starlink.' The caps have been in place since Oct 13. Trump on Friday: if Ukraine still faced a problem he would 'straighten it out and, if necessary, speak about the matter to SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.' UK PM Burnham (Downing Street): stressed Ukraine must have 'full access' to Starlink during a Friday call with Trump. Context carried by Reuters: the Starlink trouble came after Trump announced the Russian-diesel deal and waived new Russia sanctions, told Ukraine to stop hitting Russian refineries, and said Zelensky should be replaced.
sections.what_verified: Reuters T1 wire is the only family on the Ukrainian-officials claim; Times of India/Al Jazeera/Business Standard carry relays of the same material (wire's family). The counterclaim (restored) is Trump on-record. Downing Street readout = primary source for Burnham's call.
sections.what_disputed: Trump Thursday: 'Bottom line, he put it back' (on-record); WSJ reported (via Times/Business Standard) that the system was working 'more normally' after the Trump-Musk call; Trump Friday says he'd fix any remaining problem. Rubio: Starlink access is governed by a private commercial contract, SpaceX/Musk decide. The 160 km/h cap figure is per Ukrainian officials only.
sections.why_matters: The president says the off-switch is back on; Kyiv says nothing changed. Five Ukrainian officials, the 160 km/h cap, and one British prime minister calling Washington to beg for 'full access' -- the update card on the Starlink contradiction.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE to totw-20261023-1100-03 / totw-20261023-0500-07 (Starlink saga) -- Reuters: five Ukrainian officials say the 160 km/h speed caps REMAIN since Oct 13, contradicting Trump's 'fully restored'; Trump Friday: would 'straighten it out', may call Musk; UK PM Burnham pressed Trump

totw_analysis: Our read: The president says the off-switch is back on; Kyiv says nothing changed. Five Ukrainian officials, the 160 km/h cap, and one British prime minister calling Washington to beg for 'full access' -- the update card on the Starlink contradiction. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Did Trump/Musk hand Russia an advantage by capping Ukraine's drone-defence network (betrayal) -- or is this just a private company's commercial throttle (fair business)?
